newsitem.title: PERU: Lima bolsa reopens after Wed suspension on crisis.
newsitem.headline: Lima bolsa reopens after Wed suspension on crisis.

text.p: The Lima stock exchange reopened at the normal starting time of 9 a.m. (1400 GMT) Thursday after trade was suspended Wednesday due to heavy falls following Peru's ongoing hostage crisis, bolsa officials said.

Santander Investment based in Lima recommended in a report investing in the local market because the "attack is only a specific incident and does not represent a new outbreak of violence. We see the negative reaction of the market as a good opportunity to buy."
Late Tuesday, rebels stormed the Japanese emabssador's residence in Lima and are holding up to 484 hostages, including high-ranking government officials and foreign diplomats.
The rebels say they will kill all the hostages if their comrades in prison are not released.
